article_title: The US-Canada trade war in 5 charts

tasks.prompt: What is the article's main purpose?
options: To use economic data to explain how the US-Canada tariff conflict is affecting regions, trade, jobs and consumers
To announce that the US and Canada have signed a new free-trade agreement
To argue that tariffs affect only politicians and never businesses
To compare Canada's economy exclusively with China's economy
tasks.correct_answer: To use economic data to explain how the US-Canada tariff conflict is affecting regions, trade, jobs and consumers
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה משתמשת בחמישה נושאים מבוססי נתונים כדי להמחיש את השפעות מלחמת הסחר משני צדי הגבול.

tasks.prompt: Which Canadian province has been hit hardest by US auto and steel tariffs?
options: Alberta
Ontario
Prince Edward Island
Newfoundland and Labrador
tasks.explanation_hebrew: אונטריו, שבה מגזר ייצור גדול ותעשיות רכב ופלדה, מתוארת כנפגעת ביותר.

tasks.prompt: How did Canada's average effective US tariff rate change after the latest measures?
options: It fell from 5.7% to 2.9%
It remained fixed at 20.5%
It nearly doubled from 2.9% to 5.7%
It rose above China's rate
tasks.explanation_hebrew: שיעור המכס האפקטיבי הממוצע על קנדה כמעט הוכפל מ־2.9% ל־5.7%.

tasks.prompt: Why might Canada target counter-tariffs at Ohio, Illinois and Pennsylvania?
options: Those states have no economic relationship with Canada
They are the only states allowed to export steel
Canada wants to eliminate all American agriculture
They are politically important swing states where economic pain could influence the midterm balance of power
tasks.correct_answer: They are politically important swing states where economic pain could influence the midterm balance of power
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכוונת המכסים למדינות מתנדנדות עשויה ליצור לחץ פוליטי לקראת בחירות האמצע.

tasks.prompt: What does “feel the brunt” mean when describing provinces affected by the new tariffs?
options: Receive the largest or most severe share of the impact
Avoid nearly all economic consequences
Collect tariffs directly from US households
Replace manufacturing with financial services
tasks.correct_answer: Receive the largest or most severe share of the impact
tasks.explanation_hebrew: feel the brunt פירושו לשאת בחלק העיקרי או החמור ביותר של הפגיעה.

tasks.prompt: What does “warded off recession concerns” mean in the discussion of Canada's GDP rebound?
options: Proved that recessions can never occur in Canada
Transferred the risk of recession entirely to the US
Reduced or delayed fears that the economy was entering a recession
Caused the government to stop measuring GDP
tasks.correct_answer: Reduced or delayed fears that the economy was entering a recession
tasks.explanation_hebrew: warded off פירושו הרחיק או דחה איום; הנתונים החיוביים הקטינו לעת עתה את החשש ממיתון.

tasks.prompt: Compare the regional effects of the tariffs in Canada and of Canada's retaliation in the United States.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין אזורים בולטים, ענפים שנפגעו ונתון כמותי אחד לפחות מכל צד כאשר הוא זמין.
expected_points: Ontario is heavily exposed through auto and steel production
Ontario has lost tens of thousands of manufacturing jobs since early 2025
Quebec metal exports fell 36% between February 2025 and 2026
Quebec metal-sector employment fell 3.6%
British Columbia, Quebec and Ontario are expected to feel much of the latest Canadian impact
Ohio is expected to be the US state most affected by Canada's response
C$3.2bn, or 12%, of Ohio's exports are set to face Canadian tariffs
Ohio steel and washing machines are targeted
Illinois farm and construction equipment is affected
Pennsylvania is also among the most exposed states

tasks.prompt: Why can some Canadian businesses diversify away from the US more easily than Ontario manufacturers?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר את ההבדל בין מוצר או עסק גמיש לבין שרשראות ייצור אזוריות המשולבות עמוקות בשוק האמריקאי.
expected_points: Some firms can seek customers at trade events in Europe
Outclass shifted from New York trunk shows to Paris
European consumers may be especially receptive to Canadian products
Manufacturing supply chains in Ontario are deeply integrated with the US
Auto and parts plants depend on cross-border production networks
Some regions have limited non-US export growth
Finding replacement markets may not offset broader weakness quickly
Geographic proximity and decades of free trade created structural dependence

tasks.prompt: Summarise the five major economic patterns the article identifies in the trade war.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכסות פגיעה אזורית בקנדה, מכסי תגובה בארה״ב, שיעורי מכס, גיוון יצוא והשפעה על תעסוקה והכנסה.
expected_points: Ontario and Quebec are among the Canadian regions most exposed to sectoral tariffs
Canada's counter-tariffs concentrate pain in politically important US states
Canada's average effective US tariff rate rose from 2.9% to 5.7%
The US still buys more than 70% of Canadian exports
Some Canadian firms are expanding sales outside the US
Deeply integrated Ontario manufacturers struggle to diversify
Canada attracted record recent foreign direct investment and GDP rebounded
About 55,000 Canadian manufacturing jobs were lost from January 2025 to January 2026
Up to 90,000 Canadian jobs could be lost if the newest tariffs persist
US households may pay about $840 more on average because of wider Trump tariffs

tasks.prompt: Write a balanced policy recommendation for Canada responding to the trade war. Use evidence from at least three sections of the article.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציע מדיניות באנגלית שמאזנת בין תגובה מיידית, הגנה על צרכנים, גיוון סחר ותמיכה באזורים פגיעים.
expected_points: Target retaliation strategically rather than broadly
Limit direct costs for Canadian consumers where possible
Support displaced manufacturing workers in Ontario and Quebec
Help deeply integrated regions adapt their supply chains
Promote non-US export markets over the long term
Build on firms' successful expansion into Europe
Use investment initiatives to attract new capital
Preserve the benefits of the rebound in exports and domestic investment
Prepare for higher costs on industrial inputs
Seek a negotiated resolution because prolonged tariffs threaten jobs and disposable income
